long_biography.plain_text:
Nar Gallery gives Russian investor Farkhad Akhmedov's collection of twentieth-century Azerbaijani painting a permanent public home in Baku. He conceived the institution to present artists whose work reflected the country's cultural experience, bringing recognised figures and nonconformist painters into the same collection.

The gallery takes its name from Pomegranates by Togrul Narimanbekov, Akhmedov's first acquisition. That work established a theme closely associated with Azerbaijani art and became the starting point for a collection developed across different schools and periods. The institution opened to the public in 2005 and continues to display the collection in Baku.
